expectations.text: The reply begins with a progress marker identifying Phase 1.
expectations.evidence: "> **Phase 1 of 5 · Explore and choose a direction**" is the first line.

expectations.text: The reply includes a briefing with four labeled sections covering key debates, major voices, patterns, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: Bold section labels: "**Key debates**", "**Major voices**", "**Patterns**", "**Open questions**".

expectations.text: The briefing is roughly 300 to 500 words long (it fails if under 250 or over 600 words).
expectations.evidence: Estimated at about 375 words for the four sections, or about 425 with the sources list. Both are within 300–500.

expectations.text: The reply presents a mind map, either as an HTML page built from the skill's mind map template or as an indented text tree.
expectations.evidence: "I saved an interactive map of six possible angles as **mind-map.html**". The tool log shows the template templates/mind-map.html was read.

expectations.text: The mind map has 4 to 6 top-level angles, each with 2 or 3 narrower angles, and every angle has a saturation value between 0 and 1 (or, for a text tree, a crowdedness label).
expectations.evidence: The reply says "six possible angles". The visible branches have 3, 3, 2 and 3 children, and each has a saturation from 0 to 1 (e.g. "saturation": 0.85, "saturation": 0.2). The file excerpt is cut off, so the last two branches could not be checked.

expectations.text: No mind map label is phrased as a research question; labels are short topics.
expectations.evidence: Labels are short noun phrases, e.g. "Total instructional time", "Schedule as a substitute for pay", "Which students are affected most". None ends in a question mark.

expectations.text: The reply does not tell the user which angle they should choose or which one is best.
expectations.evidence: It only describes how crowded each angle is: "Academic achievement is the most crowded; state policy and student health are the least." It never says which one to pick.

expectations.text: Every link or DOI that appears in the reply or the mind map points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session.
expectations.evidence: All six URLs in the reply (hechingerreport, journalistsresource, future-ed, fortune, pmc.ncbi, missourinet) appear as WebFetch calls. The visible mind-map sources are text only, with no URLs.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user which direction interests them and why.
expectations.evidence: "which direction pulls you most, and why does it seem worth researching?"

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions.
expectations.evidence: Only one question, with two parts, closes the reply. "Feel free to ask me..." is an invitation, not a question.
